transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-22
Start: 09:30 PST
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jordan (CSM), Ethan (SE), Sam H., Lina T., Marcus P., Nora L.

Summary:
Quick renewal/check-in to confirm retainer stretch, scope EU staging, and scope a small Private/VPC pilot. Customer interested in committed burst capacity for Q1 and wants clear KMS and audit log story. Pricing/milestones and technical runbook next.

Topics covered:
- Current usage and headroom vs committed retainer
- EU staging timeline and data residency concerns
- Private (VPC/on-prem) pilot scope and security: KMS, SSO, audit logs
- Latency vs cost tradeoffs and fallback policies
- Next steps: benchmark run, contract amendment, security artifact exchange

Action items (spoken):
- Alex: send revised pricing + sample invoice scenarios (retainer + burst)
- Priya: run throughput bench and confirm expected latency at 5k tokens/s workload
- Sam: provide VPC/CIDR and egress constraints + compliance contact

Transcript body (note: transcription imperfect, some product names and acronyms may be off):
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey thanks everyone for joining, um, appreciate you squeezing this in before the holidays. Quick roll call — who we got?
[00:08] Sam H.: Sam here, Lina, Marcus and Nora from Catamaran. Morning.
[00:12] Alex: Great. Priya, Jordan with me on the redwood side. We'll keep this tight — main goal is retainer stretch and EU staging plan.
[00:20] Priya (SE): Yeah, hi all. I'll do the tech bits. We looked at the usage you shared — thanks for the CSV dump — and there's a clear pattern of peak bursts around end-of-month for route scoring.
[00:30] Lina (Customer): Yep, those are the billing cycles for our carriers — spikes are real. We've been seeing some tail latency issues when we push more concurrent requests.
[00:38] Priya: Right. In the current hosted plan you're at about 70% of the retainer baseline but bursts exceed reserved capacity ~6–8 hours on monthly peaks. Two options—we can top up reserved capacity, or add burst credits + smarter batching.
[00:50] Sam: We're leaning toward predictable committed capacity for Q1 because we can't have fallback to slower models during peak shipping windows. Latency SLOs are business-critical.
[01:00] Alex: Understood. For committed capacity we usually recommend Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput; for EU data residency we can either stage EU geocluster in our hosted EU region or run Redwood Private (VPC) with customer networking. There's a cost delta.
[01:15] Marcus (Procurement): What's the delta roughly? We need a ballpark for procurement — dedicated vs private numbers.
[01:20] Alex: High level — Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) is mid-range premium; Private/VPC (dedicated control plane + customer VPC) adds an infra premium because of network egress and KMS integration. I'll share exact tiered pricing in the doc.
[01:32] Nora (Security): For Private, we need KMS/HSM integration and proof of zero-knowledge data handling. Also SOC2 + ISO artifacts. Can you confirm retention of logs and audit access?
[01:44] Priya: Totally. For Private we support customer-managed KMS integrations — we've onboarded KMS via KMS key policies and redwood side envelope encryption, though, um, sorry transcription may call it redwood kees — but basically HSM connectors are supported. Audit logs are retained per contract; we can set retention windows and export.
[02:01] Nora: And SSO? SAML/SCIM?
[02:04] Alex: Yes SAML SSO plus SCIM provisioning. We'll include the SSO setup doc in the package.
[02:10] Lina: On the EU staging timeline — our target is to have a pilot in the week of Jan 20, full staging by end of Feb. Is that realistic?
[02:18] Priya: For a small pilot (2 nodes / tiny cluster) week of Jan 12–20 is okay if you provide network ranges and a test account. For full staging end of Feb is doable but we need the retainer amendment and procurement sign-off earlier.
[02:30] Sam: We can aim to sign a short amendment that adds 30% retainer headroom for 6 months. We also want fallback to our on-prem model in emergencies — is cross-region failover supported?
[02:40] Priya: Yes, we do smart routing and automated fallback to compatible model variants — we'll document the failover policy. Note that failover to a cheaper quantized variant can change output quality slightly; we recommend function-level tests in the eval harness.
[02:55] Alex: Quick numbers: based on your recent traffic, adding a 30% retainer increase plus a modest burst pool should cover 95% of peaks and lower egress billing surprises via batching. I'll model three scenarios in the pricing doc.
[03:10] Marcus: Good. Procurement needs an estimate with renewal terms, min commitment, and CLINs for burst usage.
[03:17] Alex: We'll include per-token and per-embedding estimates and an invoice sample.
[03:22] Nora: Security — we also need a list of sub-processors and a data flow diagram for EU staging.
[03:27] Jordan (CSM): We'll send the sub-processor list and a redwood data flow diagram; expect it in the security pack.
[03:34] Lina: One other thing — latency target. We need 200ms p95 for the scoring path at 512 token sequences. Is that plausible?
[03:43] Priya: 200ms p95 is tight for 512 tokens at full concurrency, but with dedicated GPUs and optimized KV cache it is achievable for most of the calls — we usually size for 250–300ms p95 and tune from there. The variable is your sequence length distribution and concurrency. We can run a performance bench with your sample traffic to validate.
[04:00] Sam: Okay run the bench. We'll provide sanitized traffic.
[04:03] Priya: Great — Priya will run a bench simulating 2k concurrent users at typical token distribution, outputting p50/p95/p99 and token/sec. I'll attach the bench spreadsheet.
[04:12] Marcus: On billing: how do you handle regional pricing — separate lines for EU nodes? Do we pay egress twice?
[04:18] Alex: Usually regional capacity is billed per region; egress depends on where the model runs vs where the customer data resides — we'll make a clear example. If you host in your EU geocluster, egress is minimized.
[04:28] Nora: For compliance review we need SOC2 in the next week — is that possible?
[04:32] Alex: We can provide our SOC2 attestation and ISO summary; if you need more depth we can schedule a security deep dive with our security team in January.
[04:41] Lina: Good. Also curious about Redwood Optimize — will there be recommendations for quantization vs quality tradeoffs? We want to maintain quality for risk scoring models.
[04:50] Priya: Redwood Optimize gives model and quantization recommendations per workload. For risk scoring you probably want higher-fidelity variants and A/B evals; we can set up a small eval harness to guard against regressions when using lower-bit quantized weights.
[05:03] Sam: One last ops item — we need a clear rollback plan if latency or quality degrades after cutover.
[05:09] Priya: We'll add a rollback playbook: automatic canary rollback, traffic shift percentages, and immediate fallback to hosted variant.
[05:16] Alex: Okay, let's recap quick: Alex to share pricing scenarios and contract amendment; Priya to run perf bench and provide bench sheet; Jordan will assemble the security pack (SOC2, sub-processors, data flow); Sam to share network details and compliance contacts. We target a pilot in mid-Jan and full staging by end of Feb pending procurement.
[05:33] Marcus: Sounds good. Is there any blocker for procurement to start drafting PO?
[05:38] Alex: Not from our side once we send the amendment and sample invoice.
[05:41] Nora: One ask — can you include an SLA sled that shows latency SLOs per region?
[05:46] Alex: Yes will include latency SLO table and remediation credits.
[05:49] Jordan: I'll add a security deep-dive slot for the week of Jan 6 if that works for you.
[05:55] Sam: Jan 6 works for the security team.
[05:58] Alex: Nice, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the artifacts. Thanks everyone. Happy holidays early.
[06:05] Lina: Thanks all.
[06:07] Meeting end.

Recap (as recorded):
- Outcome: Agreement to pursue 6-month retainer stretch (+30% headroom) + small burst pool; pilot EU staging mid-Jan; full staging end-Feb contingent on contract amendment and procurement.
- Docs to be sent: pricing scenarios + sample invoice, SOC2 + sub-processor list + dataflow, perf bench results and spreadsheet, SSO/KMS integration notes, rollback playbook.

Notes about transcript quality: automatic transcription occasionally mislabels acronyms (e.g., KMS -> kees, Redwood Dedicated -> redwood dedicate). Human review recommended before gating security items.
